name: Glazed brick relief
summary: Bricks are pressed in a relief mould, glazed in colour and fired, then laid in numbered courses so that the figures form on the wall.
how: Press the brick clay into a wooden mould that carries a part of the relief.
Dry the brick and fire it once, then paint the glaze in colour fields.
Fire the brick a second time at about 950 °C so that the glaze melts.
Number the side of each brick and lay the courses in bitumen or lime mortar.

origin.note: Builders of Nebuchadnezzar II face the Ishtar Gate and the Processional Way with moulded and glazed bricks.

adoptions.via: Babylonian builders glaze moulded bricks in blue, white and yellow and set them in rows of lions, bulls and dragons.
